description: Experience the ultimate comfort food with our Classic Butter Chicken, a rich and creamy Indian delicacy. Succulent pieces of chicken are simmered in a luscious tomato-based gravy, infused with aromatic spices and finished with a swirl of butter and cream. This Murgh Makhani recipe promises an authentic taste of India, perfect for a heartwarming meal.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 minutes

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, 1 teaspoon garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until lightly browned and cooked through. Remove the chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add 2 tablespoons of butter. Once melted, add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Gravy
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato puree, soaked cashews, 1 teaspoon red chili powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have softened and the oil begins to separate.

instructions.title: Blend and Refine the Gravy
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the gravy mixture to a blender or use an immersion blender. Blend until completely smooth. If needed, add a little water to achieve a smooth consistency. Strain the gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra silky texture, pressing down on the solids.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the smooth gravy to the pan over medium heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces, sugar, and crushed kasuri methi. Stir well and simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Finally, stir in the heavy cream and the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter. Heat through gently without boiling. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot.

tips: For the silkiest gravy, always blend the tomato-onion-cashew base until completely smooth, then pass it through a fine-mesh sieve. This removes any fibrous bits.
Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your spice preference. For a vibrant red color without too much heat, use Kashmiri red chili powder.
Serve your Butter Chicken with warm naan bread, roti, or steamed basmati rice to soak up all the delicious, creamy gravy.
article:
Butter Chicken Classic Murgh Makhani: Your Guide to Indian Culinary Bliss

Few dishes evoke the warmth, richness, and comfort of Indian cuisine quite like Butter Chicken, known in Hindi as Murgh Makhani. This iconic dish, with its luscious tomato-based gravy, tender chicken, and fragrant spices, has captured the hearts and palates of food lovers worldwide. Whether you’re a seasoned cook or a culinary beginner, mastering this classic Indian chicken recipe is a rewarding journey that promises to bring the vibrant flavors of India right to your dining table. Forget takeout; with this comprehensive guide, you’ll be whipping up an authentic, restaurant-quality Butter Chicken that will impress family and friends alike.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

At its core, Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani) is a rich, creamy, and mildly spiced curry originating from Delhi, India. Its creation is often credited to Kundan Lal Gujral, a restaurateur from Moti Mahal in Peshawar (now Pakistan), who later established his restaurant in Delhi post-partition. The story goes that he needed a way to use leftover tandoori chicken, so he simmered it in a buttery, tomato-based sauce, and thus, a legend was born. The name "Murgh Makhani" literally translates to "chicken with butter," perfectly describing its key components.

The dish is characterized by its vibrant orange-red hue, velvety texture, and a delicate balance of sweet, tangy, and savory flavors. It’s less spicy than many other Indian curries, making it incredibly approachable for all palates. The chicken is typically marinated in yogurt and spices before being grilled or pan-fried, then gently folded into a luxurious sauce made from tomatoes, butter, cream, cashews, and a blend of aromatic spices like garam masala and fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). It’s a celebration of indulgence and flavor, truly a cornerstone of Indian chicken recipes.

## Ingredients You Need

To create the ultimate Butter Chicken, fresh, quality ingredients are key. Here's what you'll need:

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g (1.1 lbs) boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain whole milk yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice

For the Makhani (Butter) Sauce:
*   3 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (400g/14.5oz) can crushed tomatoes or 3-4 medium fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/4 cup raw cashews, soaked in hot water for 15 minutes (or 2 tablespoons almond flour)
*   2 green chilies, slit lengthwise (optional, adjust to taste)
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (adjust to taste)
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 teaspoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1 teaspoon sugar (or to taste, balances acidity)
*   1/2 teaspoon salt (or to taste)
*   1/2 cup water or chicken broth

For Finishing:
*   1/4 cup heavy cream (or half-and-half)
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken is a labor of love, but the steps are straightforward and rewarding.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, salt, and lemon juice. Mix well to ensure every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours for maximum flavor.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through. The chicken doesn’t need to be fully cooked at this stage, as it will simmer further in the sauce. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan, melt 3 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and green chilies (if using), and cook for another minute until fragrant.
4.  **Build the Sauce:** Add the crushed tomatoes (or pureed fresh tomatoes) to the pan. Bring to a simmer, then add the soaked cashews (or almond flour), ground cumin, ground coriander, red chili powder, garam masala, kasoori methi, sugar, and salt. Stir well to combine.
5.  **Simmer and Blend:** Pour in 1/2 cup of water or chicken broth. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing the flavors to meld. Remove from heat and let it cool slightly. Carefully transfer the sauce to a blender and blend until completely smooth. For an extra velvety texture, you can pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve.
6.  **Combine and Finish:** Return the smooth sauce to the pan. Add the cooked chicken pieces. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the sauce. Stir in the heavy cream. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. The classic Butter Chicken is now almost ready!
7.  **Garnish and Serve:** Ladle the hot Butter Chicken into serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that authentic, restaurant-quality Butter Chicken is all about a few key techniques:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The yogurt tenderizes the chicken, and the spices infuse deep flavor. Longer is better, up to 24 hours.
*   **Charred Chicken for Depth:** If you have a grill or broiler, giving the marinated chicken a slight char before adding it to the sauce adds an incredible smoky depth, mimicking the tandoor oven. If pan-frying, ensure a good sear.
*   **Smooth Sauce is a Must:** Blending the sauce thoroughly until silky smooth is crucial for the classic Butter Chicken texture. Soaking the cashews beforehand helps achieve this. For an even finer texture, pass it through a sieve.
*   **Balance of Flavors:** Butter Chicken thrives on a balance of sweet, tangy, and savory. Don't be afraid to adjust the sugar (to cut tomato acidity) and salt to your preference. A little extra butter at the end can also enhance richness.
*   **Kasoori Methi Magic:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) are non-negotiable. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their distinctive, slightly bitter, aromatic flavor that is quintessential to this dish.
*   **Slow Simmering:** Allow the sauce to simmer gently for the recommended time. This allows the spices to bloom and the flavors to deepen and meld beautifully.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments. Here are some classic suggestions to complete your Indian feast:

*   **Basmati Rice:** Fluffy, aromatic basmati rice is the perfect canvas for soaking up every drop of that rich, creamy sauce.
*   **Naan Bread:** Warm, soft naan (especially garlic naan or butter naan) is ideal for scooping up the gravy. Roti or chapati also work beautifully.
*   **Raita:** A cooling yogurt-based side dish, like cucumber raita, provides a refreshing contrast to the richness of the Butter Chicken.
*   **Salad:** A simple onion and cucumber salad with a squeeze of lemon juice can add a fresh, tangy crunch.
*   **Pickles & Chutneys:** A side of your favorite Indian pickle or mango chutney can add an extra layer of flavor complexity.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken is divine, don't hesitate to experiment with these variations and substitutions to suit your dietary needs or preferences:

*   **Vegetarian Butter Paneer:** Replace chicken with cubes of paneer (Indian cottage cheese). Marinate the paneer lightly and pan-fry until golden before adding to the sauce. Tofu or chickpeas can also be used for a vegan option.
*   **Dairy-Free/Vegan:** For a dairy-free version, substitute yogurt with a plant-based alternative (like unsweetened coconut yogurt), use coconut cream or cashew cream instead of heavy cream, and opt for vegan butter. Ensure your garam masala is dairy-free.
*   **Spice Level:** If you prefer more heat, increase the amount of red chili powder or add more fresh green chilies. For a milder version, reduce the chili powder and omit the green chilies.
*   **Healthier Twist:** Reduce the amount of butter and heavy cream, or use a lighter cream alternative. Opt for lean chicken breast. While it won't be as rich, it will still be delicious.
*   **Smoky Flavor Enhancement:** For an authentic smoky flavor without a tandoor, try the "dhungar" method: place a small heat-proof bowl in the pot with the finished curry, place a hot charcoal briquette in the bowl, drizzle a teaspoon of ghee or oil over the charcoal, and quickly cover the pot for 5-10 minutes to infuse the smoke.

Embrace the joy of cooking this classic Indian chicken recipe. The process of creating this flavorful dish is as satisfying as its first delicious bite.

Butter Chicken is more than just a meal; it's an experience, a journey through the heart of Indian flavors. With its irresistible creaminess, perfectly spiced chicken, and aromatic gravy, it’s no wonder this dish remains a global favorite. By following this detailed guide, you can confidently recreate the magic of authentic Murgh Makhani in your own kitchen. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to indulge in the rich, comforting embrace of homemade Butter Chicken – a dish that truly embodies culinary bliss.
